findings.doc_quote: Omitting it raises TypeError (no default value); an empty string raises ValueError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:~655 `if not name: raise SchedulerNameRequiredError(callable_name(func), str(trigger))`. src/hassette/exceptions.py:704 `class SchedulerNameRequiredError(HassetteError)`. HassetteError (exceptions.py:59) derives from ReconstructibleError, not ValueError. register() has the same check (scheduler.py:~558).
findings.explanation: An empty name raises SchedulerNameRequiredError, which is not a ValueError subclass. A user who writes `except ValueError` will not catch it. The TypeError claim for an omitted name is correct, because `name` is keyword-only with no default.
findings.suggested_fix: Omitting it raises TypeError (no default value); an empty string raises SchedulerNameRequiredError.

findings.doc_quote: Invoked on any exception, including CancelledError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:642 and scheduler/classes.py:243 say `...including TimeoutError, but excluding CancelledError`. src/hassette/core/command_executor.py:352 `except asyncio.CancelledError: enqueue_result_record(); raise`, so the handler is never reached. The handler block at command_executor.py:~541 only runs when `result.is_error or result.is_timed_out`.
findings.explanation: On cancellation the executor records the result and re-raises. The on_error handler is not invoked for CancelledError. It does run for ordinary exceptions and timeouts.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoked on any exception raised by the handler, including a timeout, but not on CancelledError.

findings.doc_quote: | jitter | float \| None | 0 | Random offset in seconds added to each run.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:596 `jitter: float | None = None` in schedule(). run_in, run_every, run_daily and the other run_* methods use the same `jitter: float | None = None` default.
findings.explanation: The default is None, not 0. Behavior is the same (no jitter), but the stated default does not match the signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Default column for jitter to `None`.

findings.doc_quote: triggered by hassette reload , or by config changes when automatic reloads are on
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/cli/__init__.py:74,114 `apps_app = App(name="app", ...)` and `apps_app.command(cmd_app_reload, name="reload")`. No top-level `reload` command is registered.
findings.explanation: The reload command is `hassette app reload`, not `hassette reload`.
findings.suggested_fix: triggered by `hassette app reload`, or by config changes when automatic reloads are on

summary: Most claims check out against the source: signatures and defaults for run_in, run_every, run_minutely, run_hourly, run_daily, run_cron, run_once and register; the minimum-interval ValueErrors; Once and if_past behavior; skip/replace/error semantics; and where= handling. Four errors were found. Two are high severity: an empty `name` raises SchedulerNameRequiredError, which is not a ValueError, and on_error is not invoked for CancelledError. The other two are a jitter default shown as 0 instead of None and a CLI command written as `hassette reload` instead of `hassette app reload`. I did not independently verify the replace-mode cancellation details by mode (line 155) or the cron field ranges (lines 64-68).
